item.title: The Millisecond That Could Change Cancer Treatment
item.description:
📝 BiomedicalMarch 2026MagazineFeature The Millisecond That Could Change Cancer Treatment FLASH therapy uses a precise burst of ultrahigh-power radiation to kill tumors and spare healthy tissueTom Clynes06 Mar 202613 min readThe French company Theryq is collaborating with the particle physics research facility CERN to develop FLASH radiation therapy. FLASH radiotherapy flips the conventional approach on its head, delivering a single dose of ultrahigh-power radiation in a burst that typically lasts less than one-tenth of a second. Researcher Vincent Favaudon was using a low-energy electron accelerator to study radiation chemistry.
🔗 Read more: https://spectrum.ieee.org/flash-radiotherapy
